And again, he's obtained this information - it's not specific what the source is - and he's passing it to Major Golic of the Drina Corps, so the Drina Corps and their intelligence organs can be aware of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to P1785.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I could, sorry, tender the last document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Um, we may have an objection depending on the source. Is this also from the so called Pecanac collection or some other source?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then we would object to its authenticity based on the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, the one that was from the -- not to give you any ideas, but the one that was from the Pecanac collection was the -- the Popovic document. This is actually from the Bratunac Brigade collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I was asking. Then we do not have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 04224 would be Exhibit P2114, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2114 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could now go to P1785. This is a Main Staff report to the president. And if we could go to page 4 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S just to keep up with our narrative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We see a report to the president from the Main Staff regarding Krivaja 95, mentioning Potocari was liberated. The MUP is organising ambushes. Does this reflect what was happening?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, it -- again, it's reflecting a picture at a point in time that is -- that is rapidly becoming worse for them but they don't recognise it yet. But I mean, this is part of the normal information reporting chain that's going up from the various units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that also includes the information that we see under "situation on the territory," that about 10.000 Muslims are estimated for transport that day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's now go to 65 ter 4135.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a document with the Drina Corps -- from the Drina Corps command, intelligence department, 12 July, to the Main Staff of the VRS, sector for intelligence and security. And then a long list of other people, including the MUP. And it's regarding the statement of a prisoner of war named Izudin Bektic. We see that particular information at the time. And you have spoken about this document before and it's -- I'm not so much considered at this point about the information in it, but based on the content of this document and your knowledge of the investigation, where do you think General Tolimir was, as we see from page 2, was at the time that he wrote this? And we see stamps in the later hours of 12 July.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the 13th --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I believe that at the time that this document is created, General Tolimir is physically present at the Drina Corps headquarters in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will become Exhibit P2115, 65 ter number 4135.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now can we have 65 ter 4136, a very similar document in Drina -- the command of the Drina Corps intelligence department from General Tolimir. In fact, it is the following number. The first one was their number 17/896 and this one is 17/897, dated 12 July with some late-night stamps on it, 2150, 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this -- we can see who it's to, including attention General Krstic and Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. And going to page 2 in the English, I want to ask you about this comment of General Tolimir's. It says: "Although it is very important to arrest as many members of the shattered Muslim units as possible, or liquidate them if they resist, it is equally important to note down the names of all men fit for military service who are being evacuated from the UNPROFOR base in Potocari." What do you make of this document? What -- how does this fit into your analysis and then, first of all, this reference to evacuation of men from the UNPROFOR base in Potocari? What is that, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Tolimir has not been to Potocari or Bratunac and does not have first-hand knowledge of what's going on. Clearly at this point in time, on 12 July, he understands that the plan should be, by normal procedure for the VRS, that the males would be identified, the names of the individuals who were captured or who were otherwise separated because they were of military age would be documented, primarily for the purpose of potentially trading them for Bosnian Serb soldiers who had been captured and were under the custody of the ABiH. That was a long-standing issue that the VRS had that they did not have as many captured Muslim soldiers as the Muslims had of Serb soldiers; and as a result, many VRS soldiers were languishing in detention facilities because they could not be exchanged. I also look at this - and again, I've talked about this significantly in the Tolimir trial - with respect to the fact that at this point in time, General Tolimir has not been read into the plan that we're not separating these people for the purpose of potentially exchanging them. The problem here, of course, you see is what happens when that doesn't happen, you have General Tolimir providing guidance to subordinates based on the fact that he doesn't know what the actual real plan is. And so, somewhere in the intervening hours between the time that he sends this to General Krstic and to Colonel Popovic, he'll give another order later, I think approximately 24 hours later, where I believe it becomes quite clear that he has then been told what the actual plan is for these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is it about this paragraph I just read to you that makes you think he is not read in on it, the plan to kill the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When one looks at what has been happening already at Potocari by this time, you already have, one, the separations are occurring; you have the identity documents of Bosnian Muslims who are being separated at various locations in Potocari being taken from them; and even though there is supposedly a list of individuals who are of interest to at least the Bratunac Brigade for their potential involvement in war crimes in previous months or years of the conflict, nobody is actually vetting these men against that potential list. You also have a scenario that, of course, I believe that many of the actual individuals from the Dutch Battalion have talked about, where they start to begin to witness individual killings that will continue to escalate through the day without anybody stopping them, and that will continue to also occur on the 13th. So I take it that when you look at the totality of information there, at this point in time at least the people in Potocari are aware that there's no requirement to document any of the prisoners that are being captured, they're not going to be vetted against various lists because they're all going to be executed at some point. And that at this point in time, General Tolimir, who's not been to that region, does not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So is General Tolimir's instruction to note down names of men fit for military service, is that consistent or inconsistent with the plan to kill people, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is inconsistent with the plan to kill people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One would think that the last thing that you would want is lists of individuals who were known to be in your custody and who will later end up missing. You're essentially proving to the outside world that you did have custody of these individuals, that they were either prisoners or civilian detainees who once you gained custody of them under law of the RS and under the VRS procedures, they had various rights and responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I would just enter this and we're done for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 04136 will be Exhibit P2116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2116 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Butler, I give you the same instructions as I gave to you yesterday, that is, not to speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. And the Chamber would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you are supposed to be halfway. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's one binder. I have two more, but I -- it's hard to get started, but once we get started you see we are going much quicker. So I hope to catch up. We'll definitely know more by the next two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The only thing I establish at this moment is that you've used five hours, where you indicated that you needed ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Correct. And I -- I'm worried, but I will try to keep this as targeted and as brief as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Overcome your worries and try to achieve what you said -- what you estimated you thought you would achieve in ten hours. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 5th of September, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
